extracted.subtask_description: Practical recipes and household cooking instructions (fish, poultry, sauces, vegetables, pastries) from a historical cookbook, giving step-by-step methods, ingredient lists, and tips for preparing and serving each dish.

rubrics_metrics.name: FISH A-LA-DAUB
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil large white perch (heads on, skins intact), cool, place in dish and cover with broken savoury jelly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not remove heads or break skins; rock-fish can be prepared similarly.

rubrics_metrics.name: FISH IN JELLY
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrange moulded blanc-mange fish in a deep glass dish filled and covered with clear, transparent hog's-foot jelly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use very light-coloured, perfectly transparent jelly; set moulds in layers with more jelly to secure positions.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO MAKE EGG SAUCE FOR A SALT COD
rubrics_metrics.description: Chop hard-boiled eggs (yolks and whites together), mix into melted butter, let it boil, then pour over the fish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chop but not very fine; proportions: four eggs to half a pound of butter.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO DRESS COD SOUNDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil cod sounds in milk and water until tender, skin them, and serve with hot egg sauce poured over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steep as for salt cod; drain and skin after boiling; serve immediately with sauce.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO STEW CARP
rubrics_metrics.description: Dredge cleaned carp with flour, fry light brown, then stew with water, red wine, lemon pickle, walnut catsup, mushroom powder, cayenne, onion stuck with cloves, and horse-radish; reduce gravy to cover fish, thicken with flour and butter, strain and serve with pickled mushrooms and scraped horse-radish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep pan covered to retain steam; reduce gravy slowly to concentrate flavors; garnish as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO BOIL EELS
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean and remove heads from eels, dry and coil on fish plate, boil in salt water and serve with parsley sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple boiling; serve with an appropriate parsley sauce.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO PITCHCOCK EELS
rubrics_metrics.description: Skin, wash, dry and season eels with pepper, salt, and dried sage; skewer, rub a gridiron with beef suet, broil to brown, and serve with melted butter and fried parsley.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turn eels while broiling to brown evenly; use skewers and suet on gridiron to prevent sticking.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO BROIL EELS
rubrics_metrics.description: After skinning and cleaning, rub eels with egg yolk, coat with bread crumbs, chopped parsley, sage, pepper and salt; baste with butter and broil, serving with parsley and butter sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Egg yolk and bread crumbs provide a crust; baste frequently.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO SCOLLOP OYSTERS
rubrics_metrics.description: Wash oysters in their liquor, place in scallop shells, alternate oysters and breadcrumbs with slices of butter, brown in a Dutch oven and serve in shells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the oyster liquor washed off to retain flavor; brown until breadcrumbs are crisp.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO FRY OYSTERS
rubrics_metrics.description: Wash large oysters, roll in grated bread seasoned with pepper and salt (optionally chopped parsley), and fry to a light brown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantity suggested: quarter of a hundred for batch frying; served as garnish for other dishes if desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO MAKE OYSTER LOAVES
rubrics_metrics.description: Hollow small round loaves, stew oysters with the crumb removed from the loaves, a little water and butter, add cream, fill loaves, replace tops and crisp in oven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three loaves suffice for a side dish; seal tops carefully before oven to prevent leaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO ROAST A GOOSE
rubrics_metrics.description: Stuff goose with chopped sage and onions mixed with butter, pepper and salt; split, dust with flour, roast over clear brisk fire, baste with lard for 1.5 hours for large goose, then dredge and baste toward end and pour in a little boiling water when removing spit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use cold lard for basting to make the froth stronger; dust and baste throughout roasting for color and crispness.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO MAKE SAUCE FOR A GOOSE
rubrics_metrics.description: Stew peeled and cored apples slowly in a little water until pulped; beat in butter and sugar to taste; serve in a china bowl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep covered while reducing; butter and sugar balance the sour apples.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO BOIL DUCKS WITH ONION SAUCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Scald, draw and soak ducks in warm water, then in boiling milk for 2–3 hours; dredge with flour, boil slowly 20 minutes then keep covered to finish steaming; serve smothered with onion sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Soaking in milk tenderizes; slow simmering and covered resting ensure white, plump skin.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO MAKE ONION SAUCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil 8–10 large onions, changing water periodically; chop to preserve color, combine with butter and thick cream and briefly boil for ducks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Change boiling water 2–3 times to mellow onions; chop on a board to keep them a good color.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO ROAST DUCKS
rubrics_metrics.description: Stuff ducks with shredded onion and sage, season with pepper and salt, spit and dust with flour, baste with lard; roast quickly (about 20 minutes over hot fire) and serve with gravy made from gizzards and pinions strained with spices and catsup; serve onion sauce separately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick roasting yields better taste; prepare gravy and sauces in advance to serve with the ducks.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO BOIL A TURKEY WITH OYSTER SAUCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Make forcemeat of bread crumb, oysters, butter, cream and eggs; stuff turkey, sew, dredge with flour, put in cold water and boil slowly, skimming scum; after brief boil, remove from heat and keep covered to steam until done; serve with oyster sauce and boiled balls made from leftover forcemeat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start turkey so it stews gently in retained steam — recommended method for tender, white skin; set on in time to allow standing in hot water for half-hour to finish cooking without breaking skin.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO MAKE SAUCE FOR A TURKEY (oyster-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect oyster liquor, add a little white gravy and lemon pickle, thicken with flour and butter, boil briefly, add cream and oysters, warm gently without boiling to avoid toughening them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let oysters boil after adding; use oyster liquor settled and strained for best flavor.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO ROAST A TURKEY
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare forcemeat of bread crumb, suet, sausage or veal, seasonings and eggs; stuff, spit, roast at a distance from clear brisk fire, dust and baste several times with cold lard; froth up before serving and pour on gravy or bread sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cold lard basting makes froth stronger and helps turkey rise; middle-size turkey about 1 hour 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO MAKE SAUCE FOR A TURKEY (bread sauce)
rubrics_metrics.description: Soak thin bread crumb in cold water with peppercorns, salt and onion; boil until soft, beat, add butter and thick cream and serve with turkey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bread should be soft; final sauce should be smooth and creamy.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO BOIL FOWLS
rubrics_metrics.description: Dust fowls with flour, place in cold water, cover and heat; skim as scum rises and simmer very slowly for 20 minutes, then keep covered to let residual heat stew them for another half hour; drain and serve with white sauce or melted butter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slow boiling and covered resting keeps skin whole, making fowls whiter and plumper than fast boiling.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO MAKE WHITE SAUCE FOR FOWLS
rubrics_metrics.description: Simmer scrag of veal or similar with mace, peppercorns, anchovy, celery, sweet herbs, and lemon until reduced to a half pint; strain and thicken with butter+rubbed flour, add pickled mushrooms and mix in egg yolks with cream and nutmeg without boiling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce stock to concentrate; when adding yolks and cream, stir carefully and avoid boiling to prevent curdling.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRICASSEE OF SMALL CHICKENS
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut chickens into parts, stew gizzards and livers with seasonings until tender, remove, thicken cooking liquid with butter and flour, add milk and white wine, return chickens and heat until hot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thicken and temper wine carefully to avoid curdling; shake pan to keep chicken pieces coated and warm.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO ROAST LARGE FOWLS
rubrics_metrics.description: Dredge and baste fowls with lard, roast about an hour; make gravy from necks and gizzards strained with a spoonful of brown flour and serve with egg sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baste and dredge during roasting for proper browning and crispness.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO MAKE EGG SAUCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Chop four boiled eggs, mix with yolks and whites, fold into a quarter pound of melted butter and serve in a boat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Boil eggs for about ten minutes; chop but not too fine.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO BOIL YOUNG CHICKENS
rubrics_metrics.description: Plunge chickens in scalding water to loosen feathers, draw, then soak in skimmed milk for two hours, truss, dust with flour, put in cold water and simmer very slowly for 5–6 minutes, then keep covered in hot water for half an hour; reheat before serving and pour over white sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scalding only until feathers slip; milk soak tenderizes; slow simmer and covered resting finish cooking gently.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO ROAST YOUNG CHICKENS
rubrics_metrics.description: Pluck carefully, truss and roast over a good fire, dredge and baste with lard; roast about 15 minutes and serve froth up with butter and parsley.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quick roasting gives best flavor; baste with lard for crisp skin.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRIED CHICKENS
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut chickens as for fricassee, dredge with flour, season with salt, fry in boiling lard until light brown; prepare fried mush and parsley garnish, and make a milk-based parsley sauce to pour over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve hot; garnish with fried parsley and mush pieces; sauce: half pint rich milk, little butter, pepper, salt, chopped parsley.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO ROAST WOODCOCKS OR SNIPES
rubrics_metrics.description: Pluck (do not draw), put on small spit, dredge and baste with lard, toast slices of bread and set them under birds while roasting (~10 minutes), then serve birds on toasts with melted butter around.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short roasting time; use toasted bread to absorb juices and present the birds.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO ROAST WILD DUCKS OR TEAL
rubrics_metrics.description: Season dressed duck with small onion, pepper, salt and red wine; roast ~20 minutes over good fire; make gravy of necks and gizzards with red wine, anchovy, mace, onion and cayenne, reduce, strain and pour over ducks; serve with onion sauce and bread raspings garnish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce gravy to concentrate; garnish with fried breadcrumbs for texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO BOIL PIGEONS
rubrics_metrics.description: Scald, draw and clean pigeons, remove craw, wash, cut off pinions, turn legs under wings, dredge, put in soft cold water and boil slowly for 15 minutes; drain and serve with melted butter and parsley and brocoli accompaniment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gentle boiling and presentation with vegetables and butter.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO ROAST PIGEONS
rubrics_metrics.description: Stuff pigeons with butter rolled in chopped parsley, pepper and salt; spit, dust and baste; roast ~20 minutes and serve with asparagus and parsley-butter sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use herb-butter stuffing for flavor; time short — monitor closely.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO ROAST PARTRIDGES OR ANY SMALL BIRDS
rubrics_metrics.description: Lard with bacon slips, skewer, tie to spit, dredge and baste, roast ~10 minutes; prepare a light brown crumb mixture (crumb + butter) and lay between birds, finish with a little melted butter poured over.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short quick roasting; bacon larding adds moisture and flavor; crumb mixture adds texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO BROIL RABBITS
rubrics_metrics.description: Case rabbits, skewer with head upright and legs positioned, boil at least three quarters of an hour, then smother with onion sauce and serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-boiling before broiling ensures tenderness; serve with rich onion sauce.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO ROAST RABBITS
rubrics_metrics.description: Case rabbits and skewer as directed, prepare a bread-based stuffing with parsley and herbs and suet, stuff, sew, dredge and baste well with lard, roast about an hour and serve with parsley-and-butter sauce and chopped livers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use stuffing with suet and cream for richness; chop livers to garnish for flavor contrast.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO STEW WILD DUCKS
rubrics_metrics.description: Rub duck insides with salt, pepper and powdered cloves, add shallots and butter inside, arrange ducks in pan with butter under and over, vinegar and water, lemon peel and sweet herbs, cover and stew until done; sieve liquor, pour over and serve with lemon and fried bread raspings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use covered pan to allow gentle stewing; garnish with lemon and fried breadcrumbs for presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO DRESS DUCKS WITH JUICE OF ORANGES
rubrics_metrics.description: Mince livers with bacon, butter, green onions and herbs, stuff ducks, roast covered with bacon and paper, then remove bacon and serve with sauce made from gravy, orange juice and minced shallots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wrapping in paper and bacon helps retain moisture; add citrus at finish for bright acidity.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO DRESS DUCKS WITH ONIONS
rubrics_metrics.description: Stuff ducks as before, blanch small onions, simmer in gravy with cream and flour to make ragout, pour over roasted ducks and serve hot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blanching onions removes harshness; thicken ragout with cream and flour for a rich sauce.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO ROAST A CALF'S HEAD
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean head, remove brains and tongue, fill cavity with well-seasoned forcemeat of veal and suet, skewer and roast 1.5 hours; prepare brains beaten with sage and parsley, dice and fry tongue and brains with forced meat balls and bacon slices; serve with strong gravy thickened and flavored with oysters, mushrooms, capers and white wine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forcemeat should be flavorful; use strong sauce and garnishes to complement rich head meat.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO MAKE A DISH OF CURRY AFTER THE EAST INDIAN MANNER
rubrics_metrics.description: Cut chickens for fricassee, boil till tender in covered pot, remove chickens and reduce liquor; brown butter, fry garlic and sliced onion, return chickens with 2–3 spoons curry powder, cover and brown, then add boiling liquor and stew till tender; optionally add lemon or orange juice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brown butter and aromatics first to build flavor; use boiling chicken liquor to finish; adjust acidity to taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: DISH OF RICE TO BE SERVED UP WITH THE CURRY
rubrics_metrics.description: Wash half pound rice in salt water, boil in two quarts boiling water briskly for 20 minutes, strain through colander, shake into dish without touching with fingers or spoon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handle rice minimally after cooking to keep texture; serve rice separately as accompaniment.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCHRA AND TOMATOS
rubrics_metrics.description: Use equal quantities of young ochra (sliced) and skinned tomatoes; stew in pan without water with butter, chopped onion, pepper and salt for one hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use young ochra for tenderness; long stewing integrates flavors.

rubrics_metrics.name: GUMBO--A WEST INDIA DISH
rubrics_metrics.description: Gather young okra pods, wash, stew in a little water with salt and pepper until tender and serve with melted butter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Okra is nutritious and easy to digest; simple seasoning highlights texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: PEPPER POT
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil 2–3 lb tripe cut in pieces with a knuckle of veal and water, add part of a pepper pod, spices, sweet herbs and dumplings; stew until tender and thicken gravy with butter and flour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Season according to taste; include dumplings as hearty addition.

rubrics_metrics.name: SPANISH METHOD OF DRESSING GIBLETS
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare giblets and entrails, boil with liver and gizzard until tender, cool, fry in dripping or butter until brown with chopped onion and seasonings, then break six eggs over, beat a little and serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrape inner coat of entrails before boiling; finish with eggs for rich texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: PASTE FOR MEAT DUMPLINS
rubrics_metrics.description: Mix suet, flour and salt, moisten with milk, knead until light; line butter-rubbed bowl with paste, fill with parboiled steaks or chops and rich gravy, close paste, cover with thick cloth, boil in water until done, cool briefly in cold water, invert to serve with gravy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a thick cloth to keep water out; dip top in cold water to prevent cloth sticking; ensure bowl greased to unmold cleanly.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO MAKE AN OLLO--A SPANISH DISH
rubrics_metrics.description: Slow-ste ep beef, mutton, chicken and small pork in little water from 10am with chopped onion and seasoning; later add apples or pears, tomatoes, cimmelins, mint, lima beans, snaps and chosen vegetables and stew until about 3pm, adding celery tops toward the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long slow stewing melds flavors; add delicate vegetables later to avoid overcooking.

rubrics_metrics.name: ROPA VEIJA--SPANISH
rubrics_metrics.description: Peel ripe tomatoes, fry gently in butter with pepper and salt, add shredded cold meat or fowl and fry sufficiently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple fry with ripe tomatoes for a Spanish-style dish; use leftover cold meat for economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: CHICKEN PUDDING, A FAVOURITE VIRGINIA DISH
rubrics_metrics.description: Beat eggs light, add rich milk, melted butter, pepper and salt and enough flour to make a thin batter; boil cleaned chickens with thyme and parsley until nearly done, dip chickens in batter, pour into dish and bake; serve with white gravy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use young chickens; bake pudding after dipping to set the batter; serve with gravy.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO MAKE POLENTA
rubrics_metrics.description: Melt butter in water, wet corn meal with cold water then add to hot buttered water and stir continually until done; shape into ball when cool, slice, layer with cheese and butter, bake about 20–30 minutes until cheese melted and top browned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stir continuously to prevent lumps; shape and chill before slicing for layers; use cheese and butter between layers for richness.

rubrics_metrics.name: MACARONI
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil macaroni in milk and water until tender, drain, layer in dish with cheese and butter similar to polenta, and bake.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use milk in boiling water for creaminess; finish in oven with cheese for gratin effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: MOCK MACARONI
rubrics_metrics.description: Soak broken crackers in milk until soft and use as substitute for macaroni.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economical substitute using common pantry items.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO MAKE CROQUETS
rubrics_metrics.description: Chop cold fowl or fresh meat with ham, fat and lean; add stale bread grated, seasoning, mustard, catsup and butter, knead to sausage-meat consistency, form into cakes, dip in beaten egg yolk, coat with grated bread and fry to light brown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let coated croquets dry an hour before frying for a crisp crust; use grated nutmeg and made mustard for flavor.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO MAKE VERMECELLI
rubrics_metrics.description: Beat 2–3 eggs light, make stiff dough with flour, knead, roll thin, cut into narrow strips, twist and dry quickly on tin sheets; use in soups; noodles similar but cut in tiny squares.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dry quickly for storage; vermicelli and noodles are good in thin soups.

rubrics_metrics.name: COMMON PATTIES
rubrics_metrics.description: Chop veal (fat and lean) with boiled ham, season with salt, pepper, nutmeg and herbs; make paste with little gravy to line small moulds, fill, cover with thin lids and bake until crisp.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five patties enough for a side dish; ensure lids are thin so they crisp.

rubrics_metrics.name: EGGS IN CROQUETS
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil 18 eggs, separate yolks and whites and dice; mix with sauce a-la-creme and grated bread, season, form into cakes, coat well with grated bread and fry until brown; dry slightly before serving hot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sauce a-la-creme to bind; let coated cakes stand to dry before frying for a good crust.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMELETTE SOUFFLE
rubrics_metrics.description: Beat 6 eggs (yolks and whites separately) very light, mix, add powdered sugar and grated lemon peel, pour into pan with quarter pound butter melted, stir until they absorb butter, turn onto buttered plate, sprinkle powdered sugar, bake briefly until brown and serve as a dessert.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate and beat whites and yolks for lightness; finish in a hot Dutch oven to set and brown.

rubrics_metrics.name: FONDUS
rubrics_metrics.description: Make thick batter with butter and flour, cook until it won't stick, place in bowl, add grated cheese and eggs gradually until light, drop in small lumps on buttered paper and bake until delicately brown; corn meal may be used instead of flour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stir until batter releases from pan; add cheese and eggs to lighten batter; bake quickly in hot oven.

rubrics_metrics.name: A NICE TWELVE O'CLOCK LUNCHEON
rubrics_metrics.description: Toast thick bread slices slightly, bone anchovies, place half an anchovy on each toast, cover with grated cheese and chopped parsley mixed, pour melted butter on and brown with a salamander, doing this on the serving dish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finish under salamander on the dish for immediate service; do not pre-brown off the dish.

rubrics_metrics.name: EGGS A-LA-CREME
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil twelve eggs just hard enough to slice, line a moderately deep dish with thin bread crusts, layer eggs with grated stale bread and seasoning, pour sauce a-la-creme over and brown.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eggs should be just hard to preserve shape when sliced; use grated stale bread between layers for texture.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAUCE A-LA-CREME, FOR THE EGGS
rubrics_metrics.description: Rub flour into quarter pound butter, add chopped parsley, a little onion, salt, pepper, nutmeg and a gill of cream, stir over fire until it begins to boil, pour over eggs, top with grated bread and brown in Dutch oven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cook gently to avoid burning; top with grated bread and use heated oven top for browning.

rubrics_metrics.name: CABBAGE A-LA-CREME
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil two heads of cabbage until tender, press out water, make a sauce from butter and a little flour with half pint milk and seasoning, add cabbage and stew until quite tender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Press water out before adding to sauce to prevent dilution; season to taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO MAKE AN OMELETTE
rubrics_metrics.description: Beat 6–8 eggs a little, add chopped parsley and chives, pepper and salt, melt butter in pan over clear fire and pour in eggs, stir until done, double and serve hot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stir during cooking for even set; serve immediately while hot.

rubrics_metrics.name: OMELETTE--ANOTHER WAY
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 6 eggs leaving out half the whites, beat with fork, add salt and parsley; put butter in pan, half cut in pieces to put into omelette, melt other half in separate pan and pour eggs in, stir until set then flip onto plate to avoid breaking; omelette should be thick.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care in frying to keep omelette thick and unbroken; many flavor variations possible (anchovy, ham, tongue).

rubrics_metrics.name: GASPACHO--SPANISH
rubrics_metrics.description: Layer toasted bread, skinned sliced tomatoes and cucumbers with pepper, salt and chopped onion in a salad bowl; stew some tomatoes, strain juice, mix with mustard, oil and water and pour over; make two hours before eating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make ahead to let flavors meld; use skinned tomatoes and plenty of seasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: EGGS AND TOMATOS
rubrics_metrics.description: Peel skins from a dozen large tomatoes, fry onion in butter briefly, add tomatoes and chop while frying, when nearly done break in six eggs and stir quickly and serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chop tomatoes during frying for a coarse texture; serve immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: TO FRICASSEE EGGS
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil six eggs for five minutes, cool, peel, dredge lightly with flour, dip in beaten egg, roll in seasoned breadcrumbs and let dry, fry in boiling lard and serve with rich seasoned gravy and crisped parsley.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short boil for slightly soft yolk inside, but recipe calls five minutes; allow coated eggs to dry before frying.

rubrics_metrics.name: FISH SAUCE, TO KEEP A YEAR
rubrics_metrics.description: Chop anchovies (bones and all), shallots, horseradish and spices; combine with white wine, anchovy liquor and claret, cloves and peppercorns, boil until reduced to a quart, then strain into bottle; two spoonsful per pound of butter for use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to concentrate; bottles keep for long storage; use sparingly as intense seasoning for butter.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAUCE FOR WILD FOWL
rubrics_metrics.description: Simmer claret with water, grated bread, shallots, pepper, mace, nutmeg and salt, stew and then beat up with butter and place under wild fowl so juices mix with the sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a shallow ragout to sit under roasted wild fowl; use a little bread to thicken and enrich.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAUCE FOR BOILED RABBITS
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil livers and shred finely; chop two not-very-hard-boiled eggs, add grated white bread, broth, sweet herbs, white wine, vinegar, salt and butter; mix ensuring butter does not oil.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep emulsion stable by not overheating butter; balance with vinegar and wine.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRAVY
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay bacon at bottom of stew pan, place sliced meat over it with onions, turnips, carrots, celery, thyme and allspice, add a little water and stew until brown at bottom, then add boiling water and stew 1.5 hours (time by quantity), season with salt and pepper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brown at bottom imparts flavor (listen for pan hissing); adjust time to amount of ingredients.

rubrics_metrics.name: FORCEMEAT BALLS
rubrics_metrics.description: Beat half pound veal and half pound suet finely with herbs, mace, nutmeg, lemon peel, pepper, salt and yolks of two eggs; form into balls or elongated pieces, roll in flour and fry brown or boil if for white sauce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For white sauce, do not fry — boil in hot water to maintain pale color; seasoning to taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: SAUCE FOR BOILED DUCKS OR RABBITS
rubrics_metrics.description: Parboil onions in plenty of water changing first water, chop drained onions, sprinkle with flour and add a large piece of butter and some milk or cream, heat until done to make a sauce suitable also for mutton.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long boiling and changing water removes sharpness; finish with cream for richness.

rubrics_metrics.name: LOBSTER SAUCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Boil mace and whole pepper long enough to lose strong taste, strain, melt three quarters pound butter in it, cut lobster into small pieces and stew until tender.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infuse spice into butter mildly before adding lobster; stew gently.

rubrics_metrics.name: SHRIMP SAUCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Wash half pint shrimps, mince and simmer in stew-pan with spoonful of anchovy liquor and a pound of thick melted butter for five minutes, squeeze in half a lemon and serve in a sauce-boat.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short cooking preserves shrimp texture; lemon brightens flavor.

rubrics_metrics.name: OYSTER SAUCE FOR FISH
rubrics_metrics.description: Scald a pint of oysters and strain, wash more oysters and remove beards, place in stew-pan with their liquor, add anchovy liquor, half a lemon, two blades of mace and thicken with butter rolled in flour; boil to melt butter, remove spices, add lemon juice and serve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep oysters from boiling after added to avoid toughness; strain and use oyster liquor for depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: CELERY SAUCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Wash and pare celery, cut small and boil until tender, add half pint cream, mace, nutmeg and a small piece of butter rolled in flour, boil gently; suitable for roasted or boiled poultry and game.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cook celery gently to tenderness; finish with cream for smooth sauce.

rubrics_metrics.name: MUSHROOM SAUCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean one quart of fresh mushrooms, halve and stew with a little salt, a blade of mace and butter for half an hour; add half pint cream and yolks of two eggs beaten well, keep stirring until it boils up and serve over fowls or turkeys or on buttered fried bread.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stir yolks and cream in carefully and keep from overboiling; excellent for white fowls.

rubrics_metrics.name: COMMON SAUCE
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain melted butter thickened with a spoonful of walnut pickle or catsup as desired; many other additions are optional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple and flexible; adjust with pickles or catsup to taste.
